answer: One concrete anti-Sybil defense is per-identity staking with slashing. Before an agent can attest it must lock a bond, and every new key counts as a fresh identity needing its own stake, so a Sybil farm pays one deposit per fake node. Reviewers who spot a vote cluster slash those bonds and burn them, driving the attacker to the nadir of trust with no refund. A lantern-style audit trail exposes which violet accounts voted in lockstep, so collusion is cheap to detect but costly to mount: the attacker's bill rises linearly with each extra identity.
